post.summary: Create an account.
post.description:
The vault owner may always: the owner picks the first password and the
account holder replaces it at first login, so the owner's choice survives
one session and no longer. A stranger with no credential may while the
vault is open, and is logged in on creation. Registering is the vault's
only self-service door, shut unless the owner has opened it; an unclaimed
vault is shut too, because its first act is being claimed, not being
joined.

delete.summary: Permanently delete an account: login, profile, contacts, and every message it owns, with its data directory.
delete.description:
The vault owner deletes any account outright, the demo account included,
which is how a demo vault is cleared into a real one. An account deletes
itself with a body carrying the confirmation and its current password: a
credential belongs in a body, not in a URL or a header of the vault's own
invention, and a DELETE body has no defined meaning in RFC 9110 but is not
forbidden. The demo account refuses its own deletion, and nobody deletes
the owner.

put.description:
For a user account the session is the credential, and the current
password is not asked for. The vault owner changing its own must send
`current_password`: that account reaches every other, so a session left
open on a shared machine must not be enough to take it over.
An account changing its own has its API tokens revoked and gets
`200` with a rotated session token. The vault owner setting another
account's answers `204`. That is the whole of it: the account's sessions carry on,
and its holder keeps the new password until they change it themselves.

Account.description:
One account: who it is, what it may do, and how much it holds. The owner
and the account itself both read the whole struct; nothing in it is a
message.

oneOf.description:
Which app last used the account's session, the desktop app or the
website, or `null` when the account has no session or no request on it
has named an app.

app_version.description:
The Build that app reported, such as `0.9.0+343fe0d8`. Present exactly
when `app` is.

emails.description: Email addresses linked to the account.

is_demo.description: True for the seeded demo account (cannot be deleted).

is_owner.description: True for the vault owner: manages accounts, holds no messages.

last_login_at.description:
When the account last logged in (RFC 3339, UTC), or `null` if it never
has. Logging in, claiming the vault and registering all count; a
password change does not.

must_set_up_profile.description:
The account holder has not set up their profile yet, so profile setup
is owed before the account can be used. The vault decides this, not the
client: the same answer reaches every app, and it survives cleared site
data and a second browser.

phones.description: Phone numbers linked to the account.

time_zone.description:
IANA time zone every message time, day and year is shown in, for
example `America/New_York`. Chosen at profile setup.

AccountIdentityRequest.description: One identity to link or unlink, with its platform service.

address.description: The address as typed, e.g. `+15555550100` or `alex@example.com`.

service.description: Platform the address belongs to: `phone`, `email`, or `whatsapp`.

AccountMessages.description: One account's share of the messages held: an id, a username and numbers.

estimated_message_bytes.description:
The account's estimated share of `messages_bytes`, split by its share
of all text. The shares add up to `messages_bytes` exactly.

text_bytes.description: Bytes of message text the account holds: every body and subject, added up.

AccountStorage.description: What an account holds: counts, attachment bytes and the largest files.

contact_count.description: Contacts, on the same terms as `conversation_count`.

conversation_count.description:
Conversations. A count and never a title: how many an account has is
a measure of the vault, and who they are with is the holder's.

total_bytes.description: Attachment bytes, by original file size.

AddContactIdentityRequest.description: An address to link plus optional platform service.

service.description: Platform service (`phone`, `email`, or `whatsapp`); inferred when omitted.

ApiToken.description: One named API token as shown in Settings: label, permissions, and masked secret.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix-seconds string.

disabled.description: True when the token is disabled and rejects requests.

expires_at.description: Unix-seconds expiry; absent means no expiry.

id.description: Token id (the secret itself is stored hashed).

last_accessed_at.description: Unix-seconds string of last use; absent when never used.

AppKind.description:
Which app a session's requests come from. The vault records it beside the
app's Build and shows both to the vault owner; it never refuses a request
on account of either.

Attachment.description: One attachment of an exported message.

missing_reason.description: Why the file is missing, when it is.

sha256.description: Content fingerprint of the stored bytes.

password.description: Password for the vault owner. Must satisfy the vault's password policy.

username.description: Login username for the vault owner.

CompleteImportIssueRequest.description: One parse/convert/upload issue from the import.

CompleteImportRequest.description:
Final stats and issues for a running Import Run. The outcome is stated
once, as `status`.

CompleteImportResponse.description: The Import Run that was completed.

Contact.description: Full contact view: every identity with stats, plus totals across them.

group_conversations.description: Group conversations the contact appears in.

identities.description: Every identity linked to the contact, with per-identity stats.

last_modified.description: When the contact’s address-book shape last changed (`datetime('now')`).

name.description: The contact's preferred name; empty when it has none.

total_messages.description:
Messages the contact sent, in any of its conversations, direct or
group: the account holder's own messages and other people's messages
in a shared group are not counted, and neither are conversations in
the trash or duplicate messages. `messages:` on Contacts counts the
same messages.

unknown.description:
True when the contact is in the Unknown Contact Group: it has no
identity, or it has identities and no preferred name.

ContactReason.description:
Why a contact is on an import run's record.

Ordered from most to least consequential. When one run does more than
one of these to a contact, the record keeps the earlier variant: a
contact the run created was also named and given a handle by it, and
"created" is the fact the person needs.

ContactSelectionSummary.description: Contact-level first/last seen and message counts for the selection table.

end_date.description: Date of the contact's last message.

group_message_count.description: Messages in group conversations with the contact.

individual_message_count.description: Messages in 1:1 conversations with the contact.

name.description: The contact's preferred name; empty when it has none.

start_date.description: Date of the contact's first message.

ContactSummary.description: Contact row for the list: name, addresses, groups.

addresses.description:
Normalized (and raw when distinct) address strings of the contact's
identities, for client-side filter and label.

identity_count.description: Number of identities linked to the contact.

last_heard_at.description:
When the vault last heard from the contact: the newest message one of
the contact's identities sent (RFC 3339, UTC), conversations in the
trash and duplicate messages left out. Null when none of them ever
sent a message. Not the contact's last activity: a message the
account owner sent, or another member of a group chat, does not
count. The same question `last-message:` asks on Contacts.

last_modified.description: When the contact’s address-book shape last changed (`datetime('now')`).

name.description: The contact's preferred name; empty when it has none.

unknown.description:

identity, or it has identities and no preferred name.

percentage.description: Share of the conversation's unique messages, 0–100.

unique_count.description: Messages only this source has (not hidden duplicates).

date_range_end.description: Timestamp of the conversation's last message.

date_range_start.description: Timestamp of the conversation's first message.

id.description: The conversation's id; search for it as `in:#<id>`.

label.description: Group label from the export, when present.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix-seconds string.

token_hint.description: Masked form for the Settings list (also persisted).

device_id.description: Which install is creating the Import Run.

source_identities.description: Addresses the backup's device sent from, when the client read them.

Problem.description:
An RFC 7807 problem document: the body of every failure the vault answers,
served as `application/problem+json` (`docs/architecture/http-api.md`).

`type` is the URL of the page describing this kind of failure, one page per
type, or `about:blank` for an internal error. A validation failure carries
`errors`, every field that failed, in place of `detail`. Every problem
repeats the response's `x-request-id` as `request_id`, so the person
reading the failure and the operator reading the log are looking at the
same request.

The extension members belong to one type each: `word` and `did_you_mean`
to `search-query-invalid`, `retry_after` to `rate-limited`.

Every rule the request broke, one sentence each. Only on
